mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY growth exceeds 2% and S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month indicates economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% and S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases for three consecutive months and S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 2% in one month signals supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases by more than 2% and S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and CPIAUCSL YoY growth is above 3%, the combination signals an overheating economy with loose monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is below 1% and CPIAUCSL YoY growth is above 3%, and S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in one month signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases by more than 300,000 and S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When Housing Starts (HOUST) increase by more than 10% YoY and Real GDP (GDPC1) growth is above 2% YoY, the combined signal indicates strong economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 10% YoY and GDPC1 YoY growth > 2%
failure_condition: If HOUST increases by more than 10% YoY and GDPC1 YoY growth is above 2%, and S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) over three consecutive months signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases for three consecutive months and S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.
